questions.passage: Though I love my job most days, I do envy my father’s simple, convivial life sometimes; I wish I could spend an evening drinking sake with my old friends every week, reminiscing about our school days and talking about life on the farm. But in my most honest moments, I know that I could not have lived like this: I had an intense yearning to see the outside world, too intense to follow the well-trodden life path of my ancestors.
questions.prompt: Which experience does the author wish he could have every week?
questions.promptZh: 作者希望自己每周能有怎样的经历？
options: Spend each evening working at a different university.
Share an evening of sake and memories with old friends.
Leave his job permanently to farm with his father.
Travel alone to a different hot spring every week.
optionsZh: 每晚在不同的大学工作。
与老朋友共度一晚，喝清酒并回忆往事。
永久辞职，与父亲一起务农。
每周独自去一个不同的温泉。
analyses: A 原文没有说作者希望每晚在不同大学工作。
B 原文说作者希望每周与老朋友共度一个晚上，喝清酒并追忆学生时代。
C 羡慕父亲的生活不等于希望永久辞职务农；原文说他大多数时候喜欢自己的工作。
D 温泉旅行出现在父亲的经历中，不能改成作者希望每周独自前往。

vocabulary.context: 作者希望和老朋友一起回忆学生时代。
vocabulary.example: They spent the evening reminiscing about their school days.

questions.translation: 虽然大多数时候我都喜欢自己的工作，但有时的确羡慕父亲简单、热闹友好的生活；我希望每周都能与老朋友共度一晚，喝着清酒，追忆学生时代，谈谈农场生活。但最坦诚时我知道，自己不可能那样生活：我太渴望看看外面的世界，这种渴望强烈到无法沿着祖先走熟的道路生活。

evidence.quote: Though I love my job most days, I do envy my father’s simple, convivial life sometimes; I wish I could spend an evening drinking sake with my old friends every week, reminiscing about our school days and talking about life on the farm.

questions.passage: I think back to when I was graduating high school, when I was faced with the question framed in the immortal words of The Clash: “Should I stay or should I go?” It was easy, then. Just go. As I get older, though, it has become more and more difficult.
questions.prompt: At what stage does the narrator recall facing the stay-or-go question?
questions.promptZh: 叙述者回忆自己在什么时候面对留下还是离开的抉择？
options: When he was graduating from high school.
When his children were in middle and high school.
After taking a university job in New York City.
After meeting the Korean student on Staten Island.
optionsZh: 他的孩子们读初高中时。
到纽约市的大学任职之后。
在斯塔滕岛认识韩国学生之后。
analyses: A when I was graduating high school 明确限定了这一回忆的时间。
B 孩子读初高中出现在后文另一次搬迁决定中，不能移到这里。
C New York City 的任职属于更晚的人生阶段。
D 认识韩国学生发生在大学期间的暑期学习阶段，也不是本句所说的高中毕业时。

vocabulary.context: 叙述者高中毕业时面临去留抉择，而不是有人替他作出了决定。
vocabulary.example: She was faced with a difficult choice after graduation.

questions.translation: 我想起高中即将毕业的时候，当时面临的选择可用 The Clash 那句不朽的歌词来表达：“我该留下，还是该离开？”那时很容易：走就是了。但随着年龄增长，这个选择变得越来越困难。

evidence.quote: I think back to when I was graduating high school, when I was faced with the question framed in the immortal words of The Clash: “Should I stay or should I go?”

questions.passage: This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades. I imagine most of you have also asked yourselves that very same question, not just once or twice, but many times over. Some of you might be like my father: loyal, prudent, and nostalgic, prioritizing a stable life. Others may be more like me: impressionable, whimsical, and risk-taking, embracing an adventurous life.
questions.prompt: Which two areas has the stay-or-go question influenced for decades?
questions.promptZh: 几十年来，去留问题一直影响着哪两个领域？
options: His father's career and his mother's studies.
Only his teaching duties and grant applications.
His personal life and his academic research.
One brief college decision and no later choices.
optionsZh: 父亲的职业和母亲的学业。
仅他的教学职责和基金申请。
他的个人生活和学术研究。
仅一次短暂的大学抉择，此后不再涉及。
analyses: A both my personal life and my academic research 的 my 指叙述者，不能换成父母。
B only 缩小了范围，也把 personal life 排除在外。
C 原文明确并列个人生活与学术研究，并用 for decades 表示持续多年。
D at the center...for decades 不支持只影响一次短暂决定。

vocabulary.meaning: 处于……的核心；是……的中心问题
vocabulary.context: 表示去留抉择长期贯穿个人生活和学术研究，不是地理中心。
vocabulary.example: Trust is at the center of their collaboration.
collocations: at the center of a debate
at the center of one's research

questions.translation: 几十年来，这个问题一直处于我的个人生活和学术研究的中心。我想，你们大多数人也曾问过自己同样的问题，而且不止一两次，而是反复多次。有些人可能像父亲一样，忠诚、审慎而念旧，把稳定生活放在首位。另一些人也许更像我，易受触动、随性而愿意冒险，拥抱充满冒险的生活。

evidence.quote: This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades.

questions.passage: This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades. I imagine most of you have also asked yourselves that very same question, not just once or twice, but many times over. Some of you might be like my father: loyal, prudent, and nostalgic, prioritizing a stable life. Others may be more like me: impressionable, whimsical, and risk-taking, embracing an adventurous life.
questions.prompt: What does the narrator imagine about his readers?
questions.promptZh: 叙述者设想读者有过怎样的经历？
options: They have all chosen adventure over stability.
They asked him the question only once or twice.
They have never considered the question themselves.
They have repeatedly asked themselves the same question.
optionsZh: 他们都选择冒险而不是稳定。
他们只向他问过一两次这个问题。
他们从未亲自思考过这个问题。
他们曾反复向自己提出同样的问题。
analyses: A 本句只推测 most of you 思考过去留问题，没有说明所有人的选择结果。
B asked yourselves 是问自己，不是问作者；many times over 也不是仅一两次。
C also asked yourselves 与从未思考相反。
D not just once or twice, but many times over 直接支持反复自问；I imagine 表明这是叙述者的设想而非调查统计。

vocabulary.context: 强调读者可能不止一两次面对同样的去留问题，未给出具体次数。
vocabulary.example: She reconsidered the decision many times over.

questions.translation: 几十年来，这个问题一直处于我的个人生活和学术研究的中心。我想，你们大多数人也曾问过自己同样的问题，而且不止一两次，而是反复多次。有些人可能像父亲一样，忠诚、审慎而念旧，把稳定生活放在首位。另一些人也许更像我，易受触动、随性而愿意冒险，拥抱充满冒险的生活。

evidence.quote: I imagine most of you have also asked yourselves that very same question, not just once or twice, but many times over.

questions.passage: There are, of course, trade-offs between a stable life and a mobile life, a simple life and a dramatic life, a comfortable life and a challenging life, a conventional life and an unconventional life. But which one gets us closer to a good life?
questions.prompt: What is the function of the paired alternatives such as “stable” and “mobile”?
options: To establish choices whose trade-offs raise the question of a good life.
To rank all mobile lives as morally superior.
To show that the author has abandoned psychological research.
To demonstrate that all readers have already made the same choice.
analyses: A 对应 trade-offs 与结尾 good life 的提问。
B 没有道德高下排序。
C 研究问题正由此引出，不是被放弃。
D Some... Others... 明确承认读者选择不同。

evidence.quote: There are, of course, trade-offs between a stable life and a mobile life, a simple life and a dramatic life, a comfortable life and a challenging life, a conventional life and an unconventional life.
But which one gets us closer to a good life?

vocabulary.context: 稳定与流动等生活方式的利弊交换

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 当然，稳定与流动、简单与戏剧性、舒适与挑战、惯常与非惯常的人生之间，都存在取舍。但哪一种能让我们更接近美好生活呢？

questions.passage: When author Donna Tartt was asked what questions she was grappling with in her novel The Goldfinch, she said, “What is a good life?…To be happy oneself? Is it personal happiness? Or is it to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness?” Tartt’s question is profound. Should we strive to be happy? Or should we work for others’ happiness before thinking of our own?
questions.prompt: Why is Donna Tartt’s question included?
options: To prove that self-sacrifice prevents regret.
To report the results of an experiment about generosity.
To frame a tension between personal happiness and making others happy.
To establish that writers reject all forms of happiness.
analyses: A 后文还要质疑牺牲是否无悔，此处并未证明。
B 此处是小说作者的谈话，没有实验。
C 与引述及后续自问构成同一张力。
D 从疑问推成所有作家拒绝幸福，双重扩大。

evidence.quote: Should we strive to be happy? Or should we work for others’ happiness before thinking of our own?

vocabulary.context: 把他人幸福置于个人幸福之前时的代价
vocabulary.example: He built his career at the expense of his health.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 有人问作家唐娜·塔特，她在小说《金翅雀》中努力探讨什么问题。她说：“什么是美好生活？……让自己幸福吗？是个人幸福吗？还是即使牺牲自己的幸福，也要让别人幸福？”塔特的问题很深刻。我们应该努力让自己幸福吗？还是应该先为他人的幸福努力，再考虑自己的？
